items.title: 67247_J.C. Higginbotham oral history interview
items.q: So we played 'Tiger Rag' in 7 keys... That was when we went on the Cavalcade of Jazz.

ctx.x: How many times did you two work together? Just on occasion?

No, see when I first came to New York ( ? ) so, anyway ... I'm not afraid to play with nobody... we'd get to work in the morning and every morning here's Jack Teagarden about 4 o'clock after the place had closed, I caught him. O'Neil Old Dale Spencer came and got me out of bed ... ( ? ) Willie the Lion Smith nothing but the piano ... and he was playing in the Nest ( ? )

... like this and I kept him there until 8 o'clock in the morning. I said, 'You ain't going nowhere.' Played Tiger Rag in every key. Every time he'd start off, I said, 'No, you're not.' Then, you know, sometimes they have agents and that things and you don't know who's listening to you. So, he decided to get up a cavalcade for jazz and Jack, he got _______.

items.q: [INTERVIEWER] What about the so-called piano school of Harlem, people like Willie the Lion and Fats Waller and Albert Ammons?

ctx.x: Glenn Miller made the tune popular. That's Joe Garland's tune and Joe Garland is collecting the money and Joe Garland has got money like this and as long as he lives it's going to keep coming in every time he plays the record.
